item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B closely implements the frozen contract with the established multipart helper and delegates to FilesService.Add. A introduces extensive explicitly forbidden API and retry changes.","reasons":["B’s Upload has the exact requested signature, validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", ...), and routes through FilesService.Add, preserving existing option, request, decoding, and error behavior.","A directly calls Raw.Do and duplicates Add’s request/response logic, violating the requirement to route Upload through Add.","A adds association fields, numerous new FilesOption constructors, and NewFileWithFields despite the explicit prohibition on association fields and requirement to keep FilesOption behavior unchanged.","A refactors global request-body and retry semantics, including ownership/closing and Content-Length behavior, despite the contract explicitly excluding unrelated retry machinery changes and preserving Add behavior."],"risks_a":["Large out-of-scope behavioral surface across Raw.Do and all seekable request bodies.","Shared-seeker GetBody machinery is substantially more complex and less isolated than buffering Upload via the existing helper.","Upload duplicates Add logic and could drift in validation, option handling, decoding, or future maintenance."],"risks_b":["Adds an unrelated PersonsService.UploadPicture API, conflicting with scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the Files convenience API.","Upload tests do not assert uploaded content, and the retry test counts requests without verifying that the second multipart body retains filename and content.","No visible tests cover validation or propagation of source-reader failures."]}
